name: security-tenant-domain-verification-review
intent: Custom-domain ownership proof and tenant routing lifecycle
artifacts: Domain claim/challenge generation, DNS/HTTP verification, normalization, reassignment and tenant routing.
trace: Trace who controls the verification token and whether old proof can claim a different tenant/domain or survive intended ownership removal.
experiment: Use only owned domains or a local resolver fixture; compare correct proof with another owned tenant challenge and a stale ownership transition.
disproof: A DNS CNAME or validation error does not prove claimability; never claim an unowned production domain to strengthen the report.
repair: Bind proof to normalized domain, tenant and current transaction, then verify renewal/removal and rightful onboarding.
branch_decisions: Distinguish hostname normalization, current proof ownership and the tenant allowed to claim it. Old verification tokens may be invalidated or remain valid by declared policy. A dangling DNS target is not proof that a provider will accept a new claim; use only an owned domain/fixture for that transition.
operational_method: Record which DNS/HTTP proof method was accepted and how alternate methods interact. An HTTP challenge hosted by the same unverified SaaS tenant can make ownership proof circular; locate the independent domain-controlled endpoint before trusting it. Compare an owned domain under each supported method, stale proof and reassignment, without claiming another party hostname or registering its dangling resource.
